6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
76	
77	universe u
78	
79	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
80	
81	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
85	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
86	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
87	
88	noncomputable section
89	
90	/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/
91	
92	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
93	`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.
94	
95	This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
96	`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
97	under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
98	`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.
99	
100	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
101	facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
102	of a chart map is built from it. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
104	    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
105	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
106	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›
107	
108	/-! ## The restricted chart map -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
111	
112	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
113	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
114	yoneda image of the open inclusion.
115	
116	The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
117	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
118	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
119	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
120	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
121	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
122	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f
123	
124	/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
125	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.
126	
127	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
128	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
129	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
130	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
131	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.
132	
133	What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
134	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
135	expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
136	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
137	lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
138	mathematics is visible. -/
139	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
140	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
141	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
142	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
143	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
144	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV
145	
146	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
147	
148	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
149	statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
150	only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.
151	
152	**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
153	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
154	(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
155	and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
156	that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
157	beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
158	classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/
159	
160	variable (C π n) in
161	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
162	to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.
163	
164	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
165	rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
166	together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
167	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.
168	
169	Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
170	`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
171	(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
172	other. -/
173	def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
174	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
176	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
177	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
178	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)
179	
180	/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
181	give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
182	twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
183	hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
184	lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (V : D.left.Opens)
190	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
191	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
192	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h
193	
194	/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/
195	
196	/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
197	morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
198	`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
199	local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.
200	
201	Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure
202	morphism is `D.hom` (`chartHom_abelSigmaChart`, `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:212`), so a
203	restricted Abel chart over `V ⊆ D.left` has structure morphism `V.ι ≫ D.hom`. -/
204	lemma chartHom_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
205	    (V : X.Opens) {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
206	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart f V) i
207	      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by
208	  change (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f)).1 = V.ι ≫ (yonedaEquiv f).1
209	  -- Both sides are the Σ-component of the universal element restricted along `V.ι`:
210	  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
211	  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
212	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
213	  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
214	    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))
215	  refine hnat.trans ?_
216	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_map_fst (V.ι) _
217	
218	end
219	
220	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataCharts
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeAbel
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Abel chart map of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
11	
12	`JacobianData.ofCharts` consumes a family of morphisms of big-site presheaves
13	`yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C`.  This file builds such a morphism out of the two
14	things the tree already has: the Abel transformation of divisor families into the degree-zero
15	Picard functor on the slice, and a representation of the divisor functor by a scheme.
16	
17	The passage from the slice to the big site is the Σ-extension, and it is functorial in two
18	independent ways, both established here in the general categorical setting:
19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat` — the Σ-extension is functorial in the extended
21	  presheaf: a natural transformation `F ⟶ G` of presheaves on the slice `Over S` induces one
22	  of presheaves on the ambient category.
23	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.toSigmaExtension` — a representation of `F` by an
24	  object `J` of the slice induces a morphism `yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F` from the
25	  ambient yoneda presheaf of the underlying object.  A point of `J.left` over a test `V` is a
26	  map `v : V ⟶ J.left`, and it names the Σ-element whose structure morphism is `v ≫ J.hom` and
27	  whose fibre component is the universal element pulled back along `v`.
28	
29	Composing the second with the first at the Abel transformation gives the chart map.
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValueTrans` — **the Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard
34	  functor**: under the chart-index degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value
35	  `abelDiv s · sigmaFamily Z · (θ^m)⁻¹` of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` is a natural transformation
36	  `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.  Naturality is `picEtMap_chartValue`, membership is
37	  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChart` — **the Abel chart map**: given a representation of the
39	  divisor functor by a scheme `D` over `k` (a section variable — this file never constructs
40	  one), the morphism of big-site presheaves
41	  `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` sending a `D`-point to the class of the divisor
42	  family it names, twisted into degree zero.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_abelSigmaChart` — the structure morphism of the single chart of
44	  this family is the structure morphism of the representing object, so the chart hypothesis
45	  `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` of `JacobianData.ofCharts` is exactly
46	  `LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` for it.
47	
48	## What this is NOT
49	
50	This is the chart *map*, not a chart *atlas*.  Neither of the two properties
51	`JacobianData.ofCharts` needs is established here, and neither is available anywhere in the
52	tree today:
53	
54	* `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
55	  scheme** — the Abel map of a degree-`n` divisor scheme onto the Picard functor has projective
56	  spaces `|D|` as its fibres, so it is not a monomorphism, let alone an open immersion.  It
57	  becomes an open immersion only after restricting to the open locus where the fibre is a single
58	  point, i.e. where `h⁰ = 1`; that locus is the reserved `chartLocus` of `w4-datc` §3.3.
59	
60	  Two updates to this bullet, both 2026-07-29.  `chartLocus` **now exists in Lean**
61	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`, and open at a general test unconditionally), so the closing
62	  clause above — that it does not — is stale.  And the implication "not a monomorphism, hence
63	  not `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`" is a **derivation**, not an extra fact: it is
64	  `mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` (`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean`), from
65	  mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  The same file gives
66	  the criterion that makes the restricted statement provable, and
67	  `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` instantiates it here.
68	* `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc …)` is the statement that
69	  every degree-zero class is Zariski-locally the twisted class of a divisor family in the
70	  window.  Over a field this is Riemann–Roch; the relative statement is DAT-B's coverage row.
71	-/
72

74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

80	/-! ## Σ-extension plumbing (general category theory)
81	
82	Both constructions below are stated for presheaves valued in `Type v`, the hom-universe of the
83	ambient category, because that is where the ambient yoneda presheaf lives and the Σ-extension
84	must meet it. -/
85	
86	namespace CategoryTheory
87	
88	namespace Over
89	
90	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F G : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
91	
92	/-- **The Σ-extension is functorial in the extended presheaf**: a natural transformation of
93	presheaves on the slice induces one of their Σ-extensions, acting as the identity on the
94	structure-morphism component. -/
95	def sigmaExtensionNat (φ : F ⟶ G) : sigmaExtension S F ⟶ sigmaExtension S G where
96	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun x => ⟨x.1, φ.app _ x.2⟩
97	  naturality T T' g := by
98	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_
99	    obtain ⟨a, ξ⟩ := x
100	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk (g.unop ≫ a))
101	      (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (φ.naturality (Over.homMk g.unop rfl :
102	        Over.mk (g.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op) ξ)
103	
104	@[simp]
105	lemma sigmaExtensionNat_app_fst (φ : F ⟶ G) (T : Cᵒᵖ) (x : (sigmaExtension S F).obj T) :
106	    ((sigmaExtensionNat φ).app T x).1 = x.1 :=
107	  rfl
108	
109	end Over
110	
111	namespace Functor.RepresentableBy
112	
113	open Over
114	
115	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
116	
117	/-- The elementwise naturality identity behind `toSigmaExtension`, stated on the raw
118	Σ-extension transition function so that no bundled-hom coercion intervenes. -/
119	private lemma toSigmaExtension_aux {J : Over S} (α : F.RepresentableBy J)
120	    {T T' : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) (v : T ⟶ J.left) :
121	    (⟨(g ≫ v) ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk (g ≫ v) rfl)⟩ :
122	        Σ a : T' ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a)))
123	      = Over.sigmaExtensionMap S F g ⟨v ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl)⟩ := by
124	  refine sigmaExtension_ext F (Category.assoc g v J.hom) ?_
125	  show F.map (mkCongr (Category.assoc g v J.hom)).op
126	      (F.map (Over.homMk g rfl :
127	        Over.mk (g ≫ (v ≫ J.hom)) ⟶ Over.mk (v ≫ J.hom)).op
128	        (α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl))) = _
129	  rw [← Functor.map_comp_apply, ← op_comp, ← α.homEquiv_comp]
130	  refine congrArg α.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)
131	  exact congrArg (fun z : T' ⟶ T => z ≫ v) (Category.id_comp g)
132	
133	/-- **The ambient presheaf map of a slice representation**: if `F` on the slice `Over S` is
134	represented by `J`, then the ambient yoneda presheaf of `J.left` maps to the Σ-extension of `F`.

136	fibre component the universal element restricted along `v`.
137	
138	This is the input shape of mathlib's 01JJ engine: a scheme mapping to a big-site presheaf. -/
139	def toSigmaExtension {J : Over S} (α : F.RepresentableBy J) :
140	    yoneda.obj J.left ⟶ sigmaExtension S F where
141	  app _ := TypeCat.ofHom fun v => ⟨v ≫ J.hom, α.homEquiv (Over.homMk v rfl)⟩
142	  naturality _ _ g :=

148	    ((α.toSigmaExtension).app T v).1 = v ≫ J.hom :=

156	
157	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
158	
159	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
160	
161	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
162	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
163	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
164	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

166	noncomputable section
167	
168	variable (C π n) in
169	/-- **The Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard functor**: under the chart-index
170	degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` — the Abel class
171	of the divisor family, shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned
172	θ-family — is a natural transformation `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.
173	
174	The degree ledger of `degAt_chartValue` is what makes the target the degree-*zero* functor:
175	the three factors contribute `n`, `deg Z` and `−m·d₁`, which the constraint sums to zero. -/
176	def chartValueTrans (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
177	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
178	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
179	    divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C where
180	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun s => ⟨chartValue C π n m Z T.unop s,
181	    chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg T.unop s⟩
182	  naturality T T' g := by
183	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun s => ?_
184	    exact Subtype.ext ((picEtMap_chartValue C π n m Z g.unop s).symm)
185	
186	@[simp]
187	lemma chartValueTrans_app_coe (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
188	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
189	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
190	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
191	    ((chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg).app T s).1 = chartValue C π n m Z T.unop s :=
192	  rfl

194	/-! ## The Abel chart map -/
195	
196	variable (C π n) in
197	/-- **The Abel chart map** of a representation of the divisor functor: the morphism of big-site
198	presheaves `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` sending a `D`-point to the degree-zero class
199	of the divisor family that point names.
200	
201	`rep` is a *hypothesis* — this file never constructs a representation of the divisor functor;
202	that is the divisor-representability obligation of the `DivRep…` lane.  Given one, this is the
203	Abel–Jacobi map at the level of the Σ-extension, and it is the only kind of object
204	`JacobianData.ofCharts` accepts. -/
205	def abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
206	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
207	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
208	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
209	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
210	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg)
211	
212	/-- **The structure morphism of the Abel chart is that of the representing object**: for the
213	one-element family consisting of the Abel chart map, the chart structure morphism `chartHom`
214	that `JacobianData.ofCharts` reads off is `D.hom` itself.
215	
216	So the finiteness hypotheses of the producer, specialised to this chart, are exactly
217	`LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` and `CompactSpace D.left` — properties of the divisor scheme, with
218	no reference to the Picard functor. -/
219	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
220	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
221	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
222	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
223	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
224	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
225	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) i = D.hom :=
226	  Category.id_comp _

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141	
142	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# A NON-ATLAS INHABITANT OF THE `pic0TypeFunctor` REPRESENTABILITY SLOT
10	
11	**HEADLINE CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1573`), and the correction is the more
12	useful statement.**  This file first claimed to be "a second route to `JacobianData` with none
13	of the three atlas antecedents", on the strength of an enumeration of seven producers said to
14	consume the same chart family.  **That enumeration was wrong three ways**, and a lane pricing
15	work off it would be misled:
16	
17	* it *omitted* producers — `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`, `ofAbelLifts`,
18	  `ofChartsOfAbelLifts`, `ofPic0ClassSurjective`, `PicRepDatum.toJacobianData`,
19	  `toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts`, `JacobianData.baseChange`;
20	* two of the seven it *did* name take an arbitrary representation and no chart at all
21	  (`ofAbelImage`, and `toJacobianData` in the `PicRepDatum` file), so "the antecedents belong
22	  to one route" was already legible in two pre-existing signatures.  This file is **not** what
23	  blocks that inference;
24	* and `jacobianData_of_subsingleton` below **is** `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` applied to a
25	  new `rep`.  So it is not a second route to the goal at all.
26	
27	What it actually is, and this is defensible: **the first inhabitant of
28	`(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` that is not built from a chart atlas.**  Before it, the
29	only producers of that slot were `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and
30	its chart-family derivatives — every one of them carrying `IsChartUniv` and the coverage
31	instance.  The slot now has an inhabitant that carries neither, and the general constructor
32	`ofRepresentableBy` turns it into the goal object for free.
33	
34	Read that as a statement about the **slot**, not about the goal.  Census the slot you fill.
35	
36	## The mechanism
37	
38	`JacobianData` has four fields: a representing object `J`, the universal property `rep`,
39	`LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom`, and `QuasiCompact J.hom`.  Take
40	`J := Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`.  Then `J.hom` is the identity, so the two certificate fields
41	are `inferInstance` — *both* of the finiteness obligations the atlas route spends whole
42	rows on (`dat-j`, `dat-glue.atlas-hcpt`, the `hD`/`hcpt` pair) are free here, for the
43	reason that the object is the base.
44	
45	That leaves `rep`, and at the terminal object it is cheap in the other direction:
46	`Hom(T, Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k)))` is a *singleton* for every `T`, so a natural bijection with
47	`pic⁰(T)` exists exactly when `pic⁰(T)` is a singleton too.  Hence:
48	
49	**`Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)` at every test `T` ⟹ `JacobianData C`.**
50	
51	No atlas, no divisor representability, no chart certificate, no coverage, no Abel map, no
52	index finiteness.
53	
54	## What this is honestly worth
55	
56	The hypothesis is **strong** — it says the Jacobian is a point — and it is *false* for
57	every curve of positive genus.  That is not a defect of the route; it is the route's
58	content.  Three things follow that are not available without it:
59	
60	1. **The `rep` slot has a non-atlas inhabitant.**  `pic0RepresentableBy_terminal_of_subsingleton`
61	   fills `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` with no `IsChartUniv` and no coverage instance in
62	   scope, which no prior producer of that slot does.  *(This bullet used to say the file made
63	   the three antecedents "route-specific, provably"; that was the overclaim corrected at the top
64	   — two pre-existing signatures already showed it.)*
65	2. **`Genus0Terminal` gains its missing direction.**  `Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` proves
66	   a datum *plus* vanishing gives a terminal `d.J`, and its header records the vanishing
67	   implication as "the single mathematical debt of S11".  Nobody wrote the direction that
68	   *produces* the datum from the vanishing, which is the direction with no antecedents.  It
69	   is landed downstream, in `Albanese/Genus0VanishingDatum.lean` — not here, because
70	   `Genus0Terminal` imports the Abel material and this file sits below it.  Its consequence,
71	   stated at the size that is actually proved (`I-1575`): the S11 chain runs from the vanishing
72	   alone **at that carrier**, needing no datum from elsewhere.  It is *not* the claim that the
73	   leaf was gated behind `divRep` — the row already says it was not.
74	3. **A `picEt`-level sufficient condition, statable over RINGS.**  `picEt C T` is by
75	   construction a subgroup of a *product* over `T.left.affineOpens` valued in
76	   `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)`, so a subsingleton at every test *algebra* gives one at every test
77	   *object* componentwise — no cover, no gluing, no naturality
78	   (`subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`), and the converse holds by the affine comparison
79	   (`subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall`).  So the two *`picEt`* quantifiers are one hypothesis.
80	
81	   **CORRECTED (`I-1574`): this is NOT "the debt becomes a statement about rings".**  The bridge
82	   from there to the hypothesis this file actually consumes is `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine`,
83	   which runs **one way only** — as its own docstring says.  Vanishing `picEt` is strictly
84	   stronger than vanishing `pic⁰`, and the genus-0 curve is exactly a case where `pic⁰` vanishes
85	   and `picEt` need not: a degree-one class is a `picEt` class and is not degree zero.  So the
86	   ring form is a *sufficient condition*, and an attack on the real debt should target
87	   `pic0Subgroup` directly.
88	
89	## What this does NOT do
90	
91	It does not represent `pic0Functor` for a curve of positive genus, and it does not weaken
92	the genus-0 debt: deriving the vanishing hypothesis from `genus C = 0` is the curve theory
93	`Genus0Terminal`'s header isolates, and nothing here supplies it.  In particular
94	`jacobianData_of_subsingleton` is **not** a witness that `JacobianData C` is inhabited for
95	the challenge curve.
96	
97	**And the hypothesis is still UNMEASURED in this tree**, though one clause of the original note
98	has since become false and the correction narrows what remains.  Nothing here proves the
99	vanishing or its negation for any curve.  What the note *also* said — "no object in the tree
100	carries all three of `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsProper`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`" —
101	**was true when written and is now false**: `Curve/P1Curve.lean` supplies all three at
102	`P1.asOver k` for an arbitrary field, and `jacobianData_of_subsingleton (P1.asOver k) h`
103	elaborates.  So the producer below is applicable at a concrete curve; what it still lacks there
104	is the hypothesis `h`, since `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` is a cohomological computation nothing in
105	the tree performs.  The sentence above about positive genus still rests on mathematics outside
106	the formalization — `ℙ¹` is the genus-`0` object and gives no positive-genus witness — so
107	"false at positive genus" still reads as a measurement and still is not one.
108	
109	## Main declarations
110	
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableBy_terminal_of_subsingleton` — **the non-atlas inhabitant
112	  of the `rep` slot**, at the terminal object, from vanishing `pic⁰`.
113	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` — `ofRepresentableBy` applied to it.
114	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_picEt_of_affine` / `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` — the
115	  `picEt`-level reduction to test rings, componentwise, and its one-way descent to `pic⁰`.
116	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall` — the converse of the *first* of those.
117	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_affine_subsingleton` — the producer with the
118	  ring-level hypothesis.
119	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup_eq_bot_of_subsingleton` /
120	  `subsingleton_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` — the two spellings of the hypothesis are
121	  interderivable, so `Genus0Terminal`'s `= ⊥` form and this file's `Subsingleton` form are
122	  not a fork.
123	-/

126	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

142	/-! ## The two certificate fields at the terminal object
143	
144	Both are `inferInstance`, and they are recorded as named lemmas because the atlas route
145	spends two board rows on exactly these obligations (`dat-j` for `quasiCompact`,
146	`dat-glue.atlas-hcpt` for its `CompactSpace` spelling).  At this carrier they cost
147	nothing, and the reason is structural rather than lucky: the structure morphism *is* an
148	identity, so any morphism property containing identities holds. -/
149	
150	/-- `LocallyOfFiniteType` at the terminal object: the structure morphism is `𝟙`. -/
151	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_terminal :
152	    LocallyOfFiniteType (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).hom := by
153	  change LocallyOfFiniteType (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
154	  infer_instance

163	
164	variable (C) in
165	/-- **The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the terminal object as soon as it
166	vanishes.**
167	
168	The `Hom`-set `T ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))` is a singleton (`Over.mkIdTerminal`), so the
169	bijection with `pic⁰(T)` is the unique map in each direction, and both round trips are
170	`Subsingleton.elim`.  Naturality is likewise a `Subsingleton.elim`, at the *source* test:
171	this is the one place the hypothesis is needed at `T` rather than at `T'`.
172	
173	Note what is NOT assumed: no atlas, no chart, no divisor functor, no representation of
174	anything else.  The only input is that the functor's values are singletons. -/
175	def pic0RepresentableBy_terminal_of_subsingleton
176	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)) :
177	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) where
178	  homEquiv {T} :=
179	    { toFun := fun _ => 1
180	      invFun := fun _ => Over.mkIdTerminal.from T
181	      left_inv := fun _ => Over.mkIdTerminal.hom_ext _ _
182	      right_inv := fun x => @Subsingleton.elim (pic0Subgroup C T) (h T) 1 x }

190	This is `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` fed the non-atlas `rep` above and the two identity

205	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)) :

217	/-! ## The hypothesis, reduced to test RINGS
218	
219	The producer above needs a statement at every test *object* of `Over (Spec k)` — a
220	scheme-level quantifier.  This section removes it: the same hypothesis at every test
221	*algebra* suffices, and the reduction is componentwise rather than by descent.
222	
223	The reason is the vehicle chosen for `picEt` (inbox `I-0140`): `picEt C T` is *defined*
224	as a subgroup of `Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)`.  A product of
225	subsingletons is a subsingleton, and a subgroup of one is one.  So there is no cover to
226	choose, no compatibility to check, and no naturality to transport — `picEt.ext` is the
227	whole proof.
228	
229	This is worth isolating because it is the step a lane would expect to be expensive.  The
230	Zariski-sheaf machinery for `pic⁰` exists (`Pic0ZariskiSheaf.lean`,
231	`PicEtCoverBridge.lean`) and a reduction to affines through *it* would need a cover, the
232	S-lemma and the gluing seam.  None of that is needed for a *subsingleton* hypothesis,
233	because subsingleton-ness is inherited by subobjects rather than glued.
234	
235	The two `picEt`-level statements carry an `omit`, and it is a measurement rather than
236	tidying: they use **none** of the curve's geometry — not smoothness, not properness, not
237	geometric irreducibility.  A reduction that needed the curve would be a statement about
238	this particular Picard functor; these are statements about the vehicle. -/
239	
240	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
241	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
242	variable (C) in
243	/-- **The scheme-level quantifier reduces to test algebras, componentwise.**
244	
245	If `PicEtAff C A` is a subsingleton for every test algebra `A`, then `picEt C T` is a
246	subsingleton for every test object `T`.
247	
248	One line, because `picEt C T` is a subgroup of the product of the `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)`
249	and `picEt.ext` says two sections agree as soon as they agree at each affine open. -/
250	theorem subsingleton_picEt_of_affine
251	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A))
252	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (picEt C T) :=
253	  ⟨fun _ _ => picEt.ext fun U => @Subsingleton.elim _ (h Γ(T.left, U.1)) _ _⟩
254	
255	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
256	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
257	variable (C) in
258	/-- **THE CONVERSE**, so the previous lemma is an equivalence and not a weakening.
259	
260	If `picEt C T` is a subsingleton at every test object then in particular at the affine test
261	`overSpec k A`, and the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` is a bijection onto
262	`PicEtAff C A`.
263	
264	Recorded because a reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion
265	hides the gap instead of naming it.  Here the two are interderivable, so "vanishing at
266	every test ring" and "vanishing at every test object" are the *same* hypothesis, and a lane
267	may attack whichever is convenient. -/
268	theorem subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall
269	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (picEt C T))
270	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
271	  haveI := h (overSpec k A)
272	  (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv.symm.subsingleton
273	
274	variable (C) in
275	/-- **The degree-zero form**: `pic0Subgroup C T` is a subgroup of `picEt C T`, so it
276	inherits the subsingleton.
277	
278	Note the direction of the inheritance, since it is what makes the ring-level hypothesis
279	*sufficient but not necessary*: vanishing of the whole `picEt` gives vanishing of `pic⁰`,
280	never the reverse.  `picEt` does not vanish for a curve with a degree-one class even when
281	`pic⁰` does, so a lane attacking the genus-0 debt should attack `pic0Subgroup` directly and
282	use this lemma only as the cheap sufficient condition it is. -/
283	theorem subsingleton_pic0_of_affine
284	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A))
285	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) :=
286	  haveI := subsingleton_picEt_of_affine C h T
287	  ⟨fun _ _ => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
288	
289	variable (C) in
290	/-- **The producer with the ring-level hypothesis**: `JacobianData C` from vanishing at
291	every test *algebra*.
292	
293	Composite of `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` with `jacobianData_of_subsingleton`.  This is
294	the form to quote when pricing the route, because its hypothesis mentions no scheme, no
295	open, and no test object — only the plus construction at a commutative `k`-algebra. -/
296	def jacobianData_of_affine_subsingleton
297	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A)) :
298	    JacobianData C :=
299	  jacobianData_of_subsingleton C (subsingleton_pic0_of_affine C h)

302	
303	`Genus0Terminal.lean` states its input as `pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥`; this file states it as

308	theorem pic0Subgroup_eq_bot_of_subsingleton {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
309	    (h : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T)) : pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥ :=
310	  haveI := h
311	  (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall _).mpr fun x hx =>
312	    congrArg Subtype.val (Subsingleton.elim (⟨x, hx⟩ : pic0Subgroup C T) 1)

315	theorem subsingleton_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
316	    (h : pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) := by

9	/-!
10	# THE `∀ T` BINDER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST RINGS
11	
12	Two independent routes to a producer of `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` meet at one
13	hypothesis, and that hypothesis has **no producer** anywhere in the project:
14	
15	  `hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)`
16	
17	* `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` consumes it and returns a `JacobianData C`
18	  with no atlas, no chart certificate, no coverage and no divisor representability;
19	* `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` proves the seam's
20	  *coverage* antecedent at parameter `0` is **equivalent** to it.
21	
22	So `hvan` is not one route's private input; it is where the two routes' costs coincide.
23	
24	**What this file does.** It replaces the `∀ T` quantifier — over all objects of
25	`Over (Spec k)`, i.e. over all `k`-schemes — by a quantifier over commutative `k`-algebras,
26	and it proves the replacement is an **equivalence**, not a sufficient condition.
27	
28	## Why the landed reduction does not already do this
29	
30	`Pic0VanishingRoute` reduces the quantifier for `picEt` (`subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`) and
31	proves that one is an equivalence (`subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall`).  Its degree-zero
32	consequence `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` runs **one way only**, and its own docstring says
33	why that is not a repair: the hypothesis is vanishing of the whole `picEt`, which is *strictly
34	stronger* and false at any curve carrying a class of nonzero degree — including `ℙ¹`, where
35	`pic⁰` does vanish.  So the landed chain cannot be applied to the hypothesis anyone needs, in
36	either direction.  The reduction here is for `pic0Subgroup` directly and never mentions
37	`picEt` vanishing.
38	
39	## The mechanism, and why it needed no new mathematics
40	
41	Separation, not gluing.  `Subsingleton` is an equality statement, so only the *ext* half of
42	the descent is used: the affine opens of `T.left` give a morphism-form open cover of `T` by
43	the affine-open test objects `Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k Γ(T.left, U) ⟶ T`
44	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:60`), each an open immersion on the left because
45	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is; and `pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`
46	(`Picard/PicEtCoverBridge.lean:342`) says two degree-zero classes agreeing on every member
47	agree.  Under the affine hypothesis each pair of restrictions agrees for free.
48	
49	The `∃!`-gluing bridge in the same file (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`) is *not* used:
50	producing a class from local data would need the compatibility datum, and a subsingleton
51	statement never has to produce anything.  That asymmetry is the whole reason this is cheap
52	where the corresponding representability statement is not.
53	
54	## What the reduced hypothesis is, exactly
55	
56	Three equivalent spellings are given, each strictly more ring-level than the last:
57	
58	1. `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` at every `k`-algebra `A` — the direct form;
59	2. the same transported through `picEtAffineEquiv` to a separation statement about **plus
60	   classes** `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra, with the degree condition read through the
61	   comparison;
62	3. with the field points of `overSpec k A` themselves ring-level: every
63	   `t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A` **is** `Over.overSpecMap φ` for an algebra map
64	   `φ : A →ₐ[k] K` (`exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom`, `Spec.preimage` plus the tower
65	   identity).  So the surviving quantifier in (2) ranges over algebra maps into fields, and no
66	   scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in the hypothesis at all.
67	
68	## What this does NOT do
69	
70	* **It does not prove the vanishing, at any curve.**  It moves the quantifier; the
71	  mathematical content — a computation of the degree-zero relative Picard group of the curve
72	  over an arbitrary test *ring* — is untouched and remains unproduced.  In particular nothing
73	  here discharges `hvan` at `ℙ¹`, where `Curve/P1Curve.lean` supplies the three curve binders
74	  and `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`.
75	* **It does not make the hypothesis cheap.**  `infer_instance` fails on
76	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` (measured), so the reduced form has content;
77	  the reduction is a change of coordinates on a real obligation, not a discount.
78	* **It says nothing about the atlas route's own residue.**  The coverage clause at
79	  parameter `n > 0` is blocked on a spreading-out (`Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean:221-228`),
80	  which is a different obligation and is not addressed here.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_test_mem` — the affine opens of a test give a
85	  morphism-form open cover of it by affine test objects.
86	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec` — **the reduction**: vanishing at
87	  every affine test gives vanishing at every test.
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall` — **the converse**, so the
89	  two are the same hypothesis.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec` — the equivalence, bundled.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom` — every field point of an affine test is
92	  `Spec` of an algebra map, so the field-point quantifier is ring-level too.
93	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_picEtAff_sep` — the reduced hypothesis in
94	  plus-class coordinates.
95	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` — **the producer**, with the
96	  quantifier already reduced: a `JacobianData C` from vanishing at affine tests only.
97	-/

118	/-- The affine-open test object of an affine open is an open immersion on the left, because
119	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is.  Stated as an instance so that the cover lemmas of

129	This is the `hcov` hypothesis of the `PicEtCoverBridge` cover lemmas, at the one cover every
130	test object has: the affine opens form a basis, and the range of
131	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is `U` itself (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`). -/
132	theorem exists_affineOpen_test_mem (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (p : T.left) :
133	    ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens,
134	      p ∈ (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.opensRange := by
135	  obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
136	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)

139	  have hrange : Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T ⟨U, hU⟩).left.base

141	    change Set.range (hU.fromSpec).base = _
142	    exact hU.range_fromSpec
143	  change p ∈ Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T ⟨U, hU⟩).left.base

147	/-! ## The reduction of the `∀ T` binder -/
148	
149	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: if `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` is a subsingleton at every
150	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, then `pic0Subgroup C T` is a subsingleton at every test object
151	`T` — over an arbitrary base field, with no finiteness, affineness or quasi-compactness
152	hypothesis on `T`.
153	
154	Only the *separation* half of Zariski descent is used: two degree-zero classes agreeing on
155	every member of the affine-open cover agree (`pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`), and under the
156	hypothesis the restrictions to each member agree because the member's whole group is a
157	subsingleton.  Nothing is glued, so the compatibility datum that makes the corresponding
158	representability statement expensive never appears.
159	
160	Contrast `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:283`), whose hypothesis is
161	vanishing of the whole `picEt` at every test algebra: that implies this one but is strictly
162	stronger, and is false at any curve with a class of nonzero degree. -/
163	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec
164	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
165	      Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)))
166	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) :=
167	  ⟨fun _ _ => pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover
168	    (fun U : T.left.affineOpens => AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U)
169	    (exists_affineOpen_test_mem T)
170	    fun U => @Subsingleton.elim _ (h Γ(T.left, U.1)) _ _⟩
171	
172	/-- **THE CONVERSE**, so the reduction is an equivalence and not a weakening: an affine test
173	is a test.
174	
175	Recorded because a quantifier reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its
176	conclusion relocates the gap instead of naming it — which is exactly the defect of the landed
177	`picEt`-mediated chain this file replaces. -/
178	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall
179	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
180	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
181	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) :=
182	  h (overSpec k A)
183	
184	/-- **The equivalence, bundled**: "the degree-zero relative Picard group vanishes at every
185	test object" and "it vanishes at every test ring" are the *same* hypothesis.
186	
187	This is the form to quote when pricing either route to a `rep` producer: the `∀ T` binder that
188	`I-1603` calls "the whole difficulty" is not itself the difficulty — the ring-level content
189	is. -/
190	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec :
191	    (∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
192	      ↔ ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
193	          Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) :=
194	  ⟨fun h A _ _ => subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall C h A,
195	    fun h => subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec C h⟩
196	
197	/-! ## The field-point quantifier is ring-level too -/
198	
199	/-- **Every field point of an affine test is `Spec` of an algebra map.**
200	
201	`pic0Subgroup` is cut out by degree vanishing at every field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`
202	(`Pic0Functor.lean:107`), which at a general test is a morphism of schemes.  At an affine test
203	it is not: `Spec.preimage` inverts `Spec.map` on morphisms between affine schemes, and the
204	triangle over `Spec k` becomes the scalar-tower identity `algebraMap k K = φ ∘ algebraMap k A`
205	by `Spec.map_injective`.
206	
207	Together with the reduction above, this is what makes the reduced hypothesis *entirely*
208	ring-level: no scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in it. -/
209	theorem exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (A K : Type u) [CommRing A] [Field K]
210	    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
211	    ∃ phi : A →ₐ[k] K, t = Over.overSpecMap phi := by
212	  have hw : t.left ≫ (overSpec k A).hom = (overSpec k K).hom := Over.w t
213	  set psi : CommRingCat.of A ⟶ CommRingCat.of K := Spec.preimage t.left with hpsi
214	  have hmap : Spec.map psi = t.left := Spec.map_preimage t.left
215	  have htower : CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A) ≫ psi
216	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K) := by
217	    apply Spec.map_injective
218	    rw [Spec.map_comp, hmap]
219	    exact hw
220	  have hcom : ∀ r : k, psi.hom (algebraMap k A r) = algebraMap k K r := fun r =>
221	    congrArg (fun f => f r) (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom htower)
222	  refine ⟨{ __ := psi.hom, commutes' := hcom }, ?_⟩
223	  ext : 1
224	  exact hmap.symm

226	/-! ## The reduced hypothesis in plus-class coordinates -/
227	
228	/-- **The reduced hypothesis transported through the affine comparison**: a *separation*
229	statement about the plus classes `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra.
230	
231	`picEtAffineEquiv` (`PicEt.lean:235`) is a group isomorphism `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃*
232	PicEtAff C A`, so a degree-zero class of an affine test is a plus class of `A` whose
233	`degAt`-pullbacks vanish.  This is the spelling to attack: `PicEtAff C A` is the one-step étale
234	plus of the relative Picard group at a commutative ring, with no scheme-level machinery
235	between it and the hypothesis. -/
236	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_picEtAff_sep
237	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q q' : PicEtAff C A),
238	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),
239	        degAt ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm q) t = 0) →
240	      (∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A),
241	        degAt ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm q') t = 0) →
242	      q = q')
243	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
244	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
245	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
246	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective ?_
247	  refine h A (picEtAffineEquiv C A s.1) (picEtAffineEquiv C A t.1) ?_ ?_
248	  · intro K _ _ tt
249	    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
250	    exact s.2 K tt
251	  · intro K _ _ tt

25	
26	`pic0Subgroup C T` is cut out by a *degree* condition: `degAt lam t = 0` at every field point

33	point `t`, `pic0Map C t` lands the restriction *in* `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)`, where the
34	landed field-test theorem is a `Subsingleton`, so the restriction is `1` by
35	`Subsingleton.elim`.  What is left after that step mentions no degree, no χ, no divisor and no
36	chart.  It is the statement that the presheaf `picEt C ·` is **separated with respect to field

128	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),

130	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) := by
131	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
132	  have key : ∀ w : pic0Subgroup C T, (w : picEt C T) = 1 := fun w =>
133	    hrig T _ fun K _ _ tp => fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup C hg w K tp
134	  rw [key s, key t]
135	
136	/-- **THE CONVERSE**: the vanishing gives field-point rigidity.
137	
138	A class trivial at every field point has `degAt` equal to `0` at every field point — rewrite
139	the restriction to `1` and apply `degAt_one` — so it lies in `pic0Subgroup C T`, which the
140	hypothesis makes trivial.  Note this direction needs **no** genus hypothesis. -/
141	theorem rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing
142	    (hvan : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (h : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
145	      picEtMap C t lam = 1) : lam = 1 := by
146	  haveI := hvan T
147	  have hmem : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T := by
148	    intro K _ _ t
149	    rw [degAt, h K t, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
150	  have : (⟨lam, hmem⟩ : pic0Subgroup C T) = 1 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
151	  exact congrArg (fun z : pic0Subgroup C T => (z : picEt C T)) this
152	
153	/-- **THE EQUIVALENCE**: at genus `0` the degree condition cutting out `pic0Subgroup` is
154	provably idle — the vanishing at every test is exactly field-point rigidity of `picEt`.
155	
156	So a lane attacking the remaining obligation may take the rigidity form without weakening
157	anything, and should: it is the same hypothesis with the degree apparatus removed. -/
158	theorem pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0) :
159	    (∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T))
160	      ↔ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T),
161	          (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
162	            picEtMap C t lam = 1) → lam = 1 :=
163	  ⟨rigidity_of_pic0Vanishing C, subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity C hg⟩
164	
165	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the reduction fires at a curve -/
166	
167	/-- **The reduction at `ℙ¹`, with the genus hypothesis discharged.**
168	
169	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the curve binders over an arbitrary field and
170	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`, so at `ℙ¹` the *only* thing between
171	this project and a `JacobianData` through `jacobianData_of_subsingleton` is field-point rigidity
172	of `picEt (P1.asOver k) ·`.  Recorded because a conditional statement whose antecedent has no
173	witness curve is worth nothing, and this one has one. -/
174	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity (k' : Type u) [Field k']
175	    (hrig : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k'))) (lam : picEt (P1.asOver k') T),
176	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k' K] (t : overSpec k' K ⟶ T),
177	        picEtMap (P1.asOver k') t lam = 1) → lam = 1)
178	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k'))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k') T) :=
179	  AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity (C := P1.asOver k')
180	    (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k') hrig T
181	
182	end
183	
184	end AlgebraicGeometry
