6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction
7	
8	/-!
9	# FIELD-POINT RIGIDITY IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST ALGEBRAS
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` proved that at `genus C = 0` the `pic⁰` vanishing
12	`hvan` — the hypothesis both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through — is **equivalent** to
13	field-point rigidity of `picEt`:
14	
15	  `hrig`: a `picEt C T` class restricting to `1` at every field point of `T` is `1`.
16	
17	`hrig` still quantifies over all test *objects*.  This file removes that quantifier: it is
18	enough to have the statement at affine tests, in the plus-class spelling
19	
20	  `hrigAff`: a `PicEtAff C A` class with `PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1` for every `φ : A →ₐ[k] K`
21	  into a field is `1`,
22	
23	and the reduction is `rigidity_of_rigidityAff` below.  Composed with the equivalence of the
24	previous file, `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` derives the vanishing at **every**
25	test object from a statement in which no scheme, no open and no morphism of schemes occurs —
26	only commutative `k`-algebras and algebra maps into fields.
27	
28	## The mechanism
29	
30	Two independent halves, and neither is a quantifier trick.
31	
32	**The componentwise half** is the same observation that makes `subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`
33	one line: `picEt C T` is a subgroup of the *product* of the `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` over the
34	affine opens `U` of `T.left`, so `picEt.ext` reduces `lam = 1` to `lam.1 U = 1` at each `U`.
35	
36	**The field-point half is the content**, and it runs the other way: `hrigAff` at
37	`A := Γ(T.left, U)` needs the hypothesis at every algebra map `φ : Γ(T.left, U) →ₐ[k] K`, and
38	what `hrig`'s hypothesis supplies are field points of `T`.  The bridge is the *composite*
39	
40	  `Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k K ⟶ T`,
41	
42	a genuine field point of `T`, together with three coherences: `picEtMap_comp` splits the
43	restriction; `picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` turns the outer leg into `PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ`; and
44	`picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg` identifies the inner leg's value at the *top* affine open of
45	`overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` with `mapAlg` of `Over.appLEAlgHom` applied to `lam.1 U` — legitimate
46	because `⊤ ≤ fromSpec ⁻¹ᵁ U` (`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_preimage_self`,
47	`top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine` here).
48	
49	What is left is the bookkeeping identity `fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom`:
50	`Γ`-`Spec` transport composed with the `appLE` of `fromSpec` is the identity on
51	`Γ(T.left, U)`.  That is `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_app_of_le` at `le_rfl` plus
52	`ΓSpecIso.inv_hom_id`, and it is worth its own name because it is the only place where the
53	`Spec`-`Γ` adjunction enters — a consumer relating an evaluation of `picEt` to a restriction
54	along `fromSpecAffine` will need it again.
55	
56	## What this does NOT do
57	
58	* **It does not prove `hrigAff`, at any curve.**  The statement remains without a producer; what
59	  changes is that the surviving obligation is now spelled entirely in commutative algebra.
60	* **It is not the converse.**  `hrigAff` follows from `hrig` at the affine test through
61	  `picEtAffineEquiv` and `picEtAffineEquiv_naturality`, but that direction is not proved here
62	  and this file does not claim the two are interderivable.  (The corresponding claim one layer
63	  up *is* proved: `pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity`.)
64	* It says nothing at positive genus; the genus hypothesis enters only through the imported
65	  equivalence, not through anything in this file.
66	
67	## Main declarations
68	
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine` — the top affine open of
70	  `overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` lies in the `fromSpecAffine`-preimage of `U`.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom` — the `Spec`-`Γ` bookkeeping
72	  identity, isolated.
73	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rigidity_of_rigidityAff` — **the reduction**: rigidity at test algebras
74	  gives rigidity at test objects.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` — the `pic⁰` vanishing at every
76	  test object from a purely ring-level hypothesis, at genus `0`.
77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff` — the same at `ℙ¹`, with the
78	  genus hypothesis discharged.
79	-/
80	
81	set_option autoImplicit false
82	
83	universe u
84	
85	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
86	
87	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
88	
89	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
90	
91	noncomputable section
92	
93	/-! ## The two coherences the reduction needs -/
94	
95	/-- The top affine open of `overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` lies in the `fromSpecAffine`-preimage of
96	`U`: `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_preimage_self` says that preimage is *all* of it. -/
97	theorem top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine {k : Type u} [Field k] (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
98	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
99	    (overSpecTopAffine Γ(T.left, U.1)).1 ≤ (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left ⁻¹ᵁ U.1 :=
100	  le_of_eq U.2.fromSpec_preimage_self.symm
101	
102	/-- **The `Spec`-`Γ` bookkeeping identity**: transporting a section of `U` along the `appLE` of
103	`fromSpec` into the top of `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` and back through `ΓSpecIso` returns it.
104	
105	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_app_of_le` at `le_rfl` computes the `appLE` as
106	`ΓSpecIso.inv` up to restrictions along `⊤ ≤ ⊤`, which are identities; `ΓSpecIso.inv_hom_id`
107	finishes.  Isolated with a name because it is the only appearance of the adjunction in this
108	file's argument and any consumer comparing a `picEt` evaluation with a restriction along
109	`fromSpecAffine` needs it. -/
110	theorem fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
111	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
112	    (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k Γ(T.left, U.1)).toAlgHom.comp
113	        (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) U.1
114	          (overSpecTopAffine Γ(T.left, U.1)).1 (top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine T U))
115	      = AlgHom.id k Γ(T.left, U.1) := by
116	  refine AlgHom.ext fun a => ?_
117	  show (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(T.left, U.1)).hom
118	    (U.2.fromSpec.appLE U.1 ⊤ (top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine T U) a) = a
119	  rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE]
120	  simp only [U.2.fromSpec_app_of_le U.1 le_rfl, CommRingCat.comp_apply, homOfLE_refl, op_id,
121	    CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, CommRingCat.id_apply]
122	  exact ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(T.left, U.1)).inv_hom_id a
123	
124	/-! ## The reduction -/
125	
126	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
128	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
129	
130	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
131	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: field-point rigidity at every test *algebra* gives it at every test
132	*object*.
133	
134	Componentwise through `picEt.ext`; the field-point hypothesis at `Γ(T.left, U)` is supplied by
135	the composite field point `overSpecMap φ ≫ fromSpecAffine T U` of `T`, read through
136	`picEtMap_comp`, `picEtAffineEquiv_naturality`, `picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg` and the bookkeeping
137	identity above.
138	
139	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` is unused (the linter reports it): this half is `picEt`
140	bookkeeping, and the geometry enters only through the imported genus-`0` equivalence. -/
141	theorem rigidity_of_rigidityAff
142	    (hA : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q : PicEtAff C A),
143	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
144	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
145	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
146	    (h : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
147	      picEtMap C t lam = 1) : lam = 1 := by
148	  refine picEt.ext fun U => ?_
149	  rw [picEt.one_val]
150	  refine hA Γ(T.left, U.1) (lam.1 U) fun K _ _ φ => ?_
151	  -- the composite field point of `T`
152	  have h1 : picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam = 1 :=
153	    h K (Over.overSpecMap φ ≫ Over.fromSpecAffine T U)
154	  rw [picEtMap_comp] at h1
155	  have h3 := congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C K) h1
156	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, map_one, picEtAffineEquiv_apply, picEtMap_val,
157	    picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam
158	      (top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine T U)] at h3
159	  refine Eq.trans ?_ h3
160	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ) ?_
161	  set ψ := Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) U.1
162	    (overSpecTopAffine Γ(T.left, U.1)).1 (top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine T U) with hψ
163	  set e := (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k Γ(T.left, U.1)).toAlgHom with he
164	  have hcomp : e.comp ψ = AlgHom.id k Γ(T.left, U.1) := by
165	    rw [he, hψ]
166	    exact fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom T U
167	  calc lam.1 U = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (AlgHom.id k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (lam.1 U) :=
168	        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_id C (lam.1 U)).symm
169	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (e.comp ψ) (lam.1 U) := by rw [hcomp]
170	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C e (PicEtAff.mapAlg C ψ (lam.1 U)) :=
171	        PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C ψ e (lam.1 U)
172	
173	/-- **THE `pic⁰` VANISHING FROM A PURELY RING-LEVEL HYPOTHESIS**, at genus `0`.
174	
175	The hypothesis mentions no scheme, no open and no morphism of schemes: only commutative
176	`k`-algebras `A`, plus classes of `A`, and algebra maps `A →ₐ[k] K` into fields.  Composite of
177	`rigidity_of_rigidityAff` with `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity`. -/
178	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff (hg : genus C = 0)
179	    (hA : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q : PicEtAff C A),
180	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
181	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
182	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C T) :=
183	  subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidity C hg (rigidity_of_rigidityAff C hA) T
184	
185	/-- **`JacobianData` from the ring-level rigidity hypothesis**, at genus `0`.
186	
187	`Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` consumes the vanishing with no atlas, no
188	chart certificate, no coverage and no divisor representability, so this is the whole distance
189	from `hrigAff` to the goal object at a genus-`0` curve. -/
190	def jacobianData_of_rigidityAff (hg : genus C = 0)
191	    (hA : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (q : PicEtAff C A),
192	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
193	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1) : JacobianData C :=
194	  jacobianData_of_subsingleton C (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff C hg hA)
195	
196	end
197	
198	/-- **The ring-level reduction at `ℙ¹`, with the genus hypothesis discharged.** -/
199	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff (k' : Type u) [Field k']
200	    (hA : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k' A] (q : PicEtAff (P1.asOver k') A),
201	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k' K] (φ : A →ₐ[k'] K),
202	        PicEtAff.mapAlg (P1.asOver k') φ q = 1) → q = 1)
203	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k'))) : Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k') T) :=
204	  AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_rigidityAff (C := P1.asOver k')
205	    (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k') hA T
206	
207	end AlgebraicGeometry
208

181	`Equiv.equivOfSubsingletonOfSubsingleton` and `homEquiv_comp` holds because the target is a
182	subsingleton.
183	
184	**This is the first inhabitant of the `rep` slot at any parameter.**  `mixedParamChart`,
185	`abelSigmaChart`, `IsChartUniv` and the rest of the `Pic0Chart*` cluster all take
186	`rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D` as a hypothesis, and until now nothing produced
187	one, so every statement quantified over it was true but untested.
188	
189	*No count is given here on purpose.*  Two reasonable methods disagree — `grep -c "rep :
190	(divFunctor"` over `AlgebraicJacobian/` and a per-declaration census of header binders differ by
191	about a third, and the task brief that prompted this work quoted a third figure again.  The
192	claim that matters is a zero, not a large number: **the producer side was empty**, verified by
193	reading the three existing `…representableBy` declarations
194	(`DivRepGlobalData.representableBy`, `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause`,
195	`DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy`), each of which takes an unwitnessed structure whose only

199	`nn i = 0` still needs a legal index `Z i` of degree `m·d₁ − 0`, and the coverage antecedent is
200	untouched.
201	
202	What *is* known against this parameter, at the strength it actually has:
203	`not_mem_chartLocus_of_two_le_genus_zero_param`
204	(`Picard/Pic0ChartSubsingletonCollapse.lean`) proves the **chart locus** at `n = 0` is empty
205	once `g ≥ 2`, from the rank formula `h⁰ = n + 1 − g` of `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusH0Rank.lean`
206	(at `0` it reads `1 − g ≤ −1` with `h⁰` a cast natural), under that theorem's own `hlam` and
207	`hχ` hypotheses.  So the **`chartLocus`-mediated** route to coverage is dead here.
208	
209	**An earlier draft of this paragraph — and both of my commit messages — instead said "coverage
210	is provably impossible at `n = 0`", and that is not a theorem.**  `PointwiseCoverage`
211	(`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:99`) quantifies over an *arbitrary* open `W ∋ t` and never
212	mentions `chartLocus`; `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` calls `chartLocusOpens` only the
213	*intended* instantiation; and `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean:52-55` states outright that the two
214	carriers do not meet and that **no declaration in the tree relates them**.  So "coverage needs
215	the locus inhabited" is a missing implication, not a step.  The overclaim ran against my own
216	result, which is exactly why it read as audited — and it would have told a later lane not to
217	try an `n = 0` coverage route that is not in fact refuted.
218	
219	The honest joint statement: an inhabited `rep` at `n = 0`, where the known coverage route is
220	dead for `g ≥ 2`, and unconditional coverage at `n = M·δ + g`, where `rep` has no producer —
221	opposite sides of one rank inequality, with nothing connecting them.  A reader taking this
222	definition as a step toward representability of `Pic⁰` would be wrong.
223	
224	What it *is* usable for immediately is pic-c's `abel-noninj` fork, whose antecedent is exactly
225	`Subsingleton ((divFunctor C π n).obj (op T))`: at this parameter the Abel chart is a
226	monomorphism, `D` is terminal, and the whole `V`-interval collapses to `{⊥, ⊤}`. -/
227	def divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy :

233	      right_inv := fun _ =>

235	  homEquiv_comp {T _} _ _ :=

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40

10	/-!
11	# `pic⁰` VANISHES AT EVERY FIELD TEST, AT GENUS `0`
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T` binder of the degree-zero Picard
14	vanishing is *equivalent* to the same statement at affine tests `overSpec k A`.  This file
15	discharges every **field** instance of that: at `genus C = 0`,
16	
17	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K))` for every field extension `K/k`.
18	
19	`hvan` is the hypothesis that `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` turns into a
20	`JacobianData` and that `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff`
21	shows *is* the seam's coverage antecedent at parameter `0`.  It therefore now has all of its
22	field instances closed on a genus-`0` curve, and only its **ring** instances open.
23	
24	**A COUNT CORRECTED.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called `hvan` "the hypothesis with
25	93 consumers and no producer".  That figure is from the task brief and is about
26	`JacobianData.rep`, a *different* object; restating it here made it look like a measurement of
27	`hvan`.  Measured at HEAD: the `hvan`-shaped binder occurs in **3** files, `pic0Subgroup` is
28	mentioned in 50, and `RepresentableBy` occurs 392 times.  What matters about `hvan` is not a
29	count but that both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through it and neither had an
30	instance; do not quote a number from this header — run the grep.
31	
32	## The two steps, and what each costs
33	
34	**Step 1, through the plus construction** (`eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero`).  A plus
35	class of `PicEtAff C K` is `mk E x` for some étale cover `E` of `K`; its degree is by
36	definition read on a finite separable *field* refinement of `E`
37	(`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), and `Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero` kills the transported class there.
38	Transport back is free: `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` says the plus class does not change along a
39	refinement, and `PicEtAff.mk_one` closes it.
40	
41	Note what is *not* needed: **no surjectivity of the plus unit**.  The landed
42	`PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` (`EffectivityClose.lean:141`) requires a curve section
43	over the test field, which this project constructs nowhere; the argument here never asks
44	whether the class comes from `relPic C (overSpec k K)` itself, only what happens on its own
45	cover carrier.  So the field case needs no rational point.
46	
47	**Step 2, off the degree condition** (`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`).
48	Membership in `pic0Subgroup` quantifies over *all* field points of the test; at an affine test
49	over a field, the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` is one of them, and `degAt` at the identity is
50	`degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So a single instantiation of the membership binder
51	supplies the hypothesis of step 1 — the other field points are not consulted.
52	
53	## What remains, stated exactly
54	
55	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
56	
57	for `A` **not** a field.  That is fibrewise-degree-zero implies globally trivial over a base
58	ring, i.e. cohomology and base change; nothing in this tree proves it, and it is the whole
59	remaining distance from here to a `JacobianData` at a genus-`0` curve via
60	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton`.
61	
62	Two things this does **not** do, to forestall the obvious misreadings:
63	
64	* it does not compute `Pic(ℙ¹)` or any Picard group — degree-zero classes are killed without
65	  identifying the group they sit in;
66	* it says nothing at positive genus, and exhibits no positive-genus curve.
67	
68	## Main declarations
69	
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` — a plus class of degree `0` over
71	  a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.  Needs no curve section.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero` — **the field-test
73	  vanishing**.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field` — **non-vacuity at a real
75	  curve**: the same at `P1.asOver k` with *no hypothesis at all*, since
76	  `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field.
77	
78	Both are stated with **three** curve binders: `GeometricallyReduced` is unused in each
79	(measured — the linter reports it), even though the surrounding `picEt` descent material
80	carries four.
81	-/

98	/-- **A plus class of degree zero over a field test is trivial, at genus `0`.**

100	`degAff` is *defined* by reading the relative degree on a finite separable field refinement of
101	the class's own cover (`PicEtAff.degAff_mk`), which is exactly where the field layer
102	`relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` applies.  Transport back to the original
103	cover is free — `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap` — so no comparison between covers is needed.

106	surjectivity `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` is not used, because the argument works on

108	theorem eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
109	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
110	    (q : PicEtAff C K) (hq : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K q = 0) : q = 1 := by

113	    obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
114	    letI := hLf; letI := hLa; letI := hLfin; letI := hLsep
115	    letI : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
116	    haveI : IsScalarTower k K L := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
117	    -- the degree is the relative degree of the transported representative over `L`
118	    have hdeg : relPicDeg (C := C) L (relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
119	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) = 0 := by
120	      rw [← PicEtAff.degAff_mk (C := C) (K := K) E x L j]
121	      exact hq

123	        (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) = 1 :=
124	      relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C L hg _ hdeg
125	    -- transport to the field cover does not change the plus class
126	    have hstep : PicEtAff.mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L)
127	        (descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j) x)
128	        = PicEtAff.mk C E x := PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C _ x
129	    rw [← hstep]
130	    convert PicEtAff.mk_one C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L) using 2
131	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
132	    rw [descentMap_coe]
133	    have hcomp :
134	        ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.comp j).restrictScalars k
135	          = ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
136	            (j.restrictScalars k) := rfl
137	    rw [hcomp, relPicAlgMap_comp, htriv, map_one]
138	    rfl

141	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
142	/-- **THE FIELD-TEST VANISHING**: at `genus C = 0`, the degree-zero Picard group of the curve
143	vanishes at every affine test over a *field*.
144	
145	Only **one** field point of the test is consulted — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)`, at which
146	`degAt` is `degAff` of the class by `picEtMap_id`.  So the `∀ K, ∀ t` binder of
147	`pic0Subgroup`'s membership is used at a single instantiation, and the remaining field points
148	carry no weight in this direction. -/
149	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero
150	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0) :
151	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) := by
152	  refine ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext ?_⟩
153	  refine (picEtAffineEquiv C K).injective ?_
154	  have hs : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) = 0 := by
155	    have h := s.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
156	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
157	  have ht : PicEtAff.degAff (C := C) K (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) = 0 := by
158	    have h := t.2 K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
159	    rwa [degAt, picEtMap_id] at h
160	  have h1 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K s.1) hs
161	  have h2 := eq_one_of_degAff_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg (picEtAffineEquiv C K t.1) ht
162	  exact h1.trans h2.symm

168	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` gives `P1.asOver k` the three curve binders over an arbitrary field and

172	theorem P1.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field
173	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
174	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k K)) :=
175	  subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) K

        ((Category.assoc _ _ _).trans
          (congrArg (fun q => (eKL ≫ eLM ≫ g) ≫ q) hprod)).symm
  have hfst : eKM ≫ fM = (eKL ≫ eLM ≫ g) ≫ fM := by
    apply Limits.pullback.hom_ext
    · exact hprojC
    · exact hprojM
  apply (Over.isPullback_left CM (overSpec M B)).hom_ext
  · exact hfst
  · exact hsnd

/-- The inverse affine base-field shuffle over a scalar tower is the composite of the two
successive inverse shuffles and transport along the frozen curve comparison. -/
theorem PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle_symm_tower
    (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] [Algebra L B] [Algebra M B]
    [IsScalarTower k L B] [IsScalarTower L M B] [IsScalarTower k M B]
    (a : PicEtAff ((baseChange k M).obj C) B) :
    (PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle k M C B).symm a =
      (PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle k L C B).symm
        ((PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) B).symm
          (PicEtAff.curveMap B ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C).inv a)) := by
  let g : (baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C) ⟶ (baseChange k M).obj C :=
    ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C).inv
  change (crossBaseTransportFamilyInv k M C).picEtAffHom B a =
    (crossBaseTransportFamilyInv k L C).picEtAffHom B
      ((crossBaseTransportFamilyInv L M ((baseChange k L).obj C)).picEtAffHom B
        ((curveTransportFamily g).picEtAffHom B a))
  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
  | mk U x =>
    rw [RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom_mk, RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom_mk,
      RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom_mk, RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom_mk]
    refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C U) (Subtype.ext ?_)
    rw [RelPicTransportFamily.descentHom_coe, RelPicTransportFamily.descentHom_coe,
      RelPicTransportFamily.descentHom_coe, RelPicTransportFamily.descentHom_coe]
    generalize (x : relPic ((baseChange k M).obj C) (overSpec M U.Carrier)) = y

10	/-!
11	# THE FIELD-TEST LAYER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING, AT GENUS `0`
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` reduces the `∀ T` binder of the degree-zero Picard
14	vanishing to an equivalent statement about test *rings*.  This file closes the **field** case
15	of that statement at genus `0`, for an arbitrary base field and every field extension.
16	
17	The content is `RiemannRoch/GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`
18	transported to the carrier `relPicDeg` actually reads: `relPic C (overSpec k L)`, the Čech
19	Picard group of the base-changed curve modulo classes pulled back from the base.
20	
21	## Why the base change is the whole plumbing cost
22	
23	`relPicDeg L` is a homomorphism out of `relPic C (overSpec k L)`, whose representatives are
24	Čech classes on `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` — the curve base-changed to `L`, *not* `C`.  So the
25	`χ = 1` hypothesis has to hold at the base-changed curve at **every** field extension, and
26	`genus C = 0` is a statement about `C` over `k`.
27	
28	That transport is landed and needs no new cohomology: `finrank_h0_baseField` and
29	`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` (`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:353,363`) compute both
30	Betti numbers of the base-changed curve, and `h0_moduleKSheaf` gives `h⁰ = 1` over `k`.  Then
31	`χ = h⁰ - h¹ = 1 - genus C = 1`.
32	
33	Why *these* lemmas: they are stated at `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.moduleKSheaf L` under
34	`instOverBaseChange` (`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean:74`), which is the key `relPicDeg`'s
35	degree stack consumes, so no transport is needed.
36	
37	**RETRACTED CLAIM, and it was published as a prohibition.**  An earlier version of this
38	paragraph said that going through `chi_moduleKSheaf` at the bundled `baseChangeBundle C L`
39	gives the same object under a different `Over` instance and that "the resulting `chi` terms do
40	not unify — measured".  **That is false.**  The bundled route closes at default heartbeats once
41	a `change` to the bundled spelling precedes the `simpa`; what was actually measured was one
42	`simpa` failing *without* that step, i.e. a fact about a tactic call, restated as a fact about
43	two objects.  `Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean` (pic-g) does it the bundled way at `ℙ¹`.  Both
44	routes work; this one is not the only one and nothing here forecloses the other.
45	
46	## What this does NOT do
47	
48	* **It is not the vanishing.**  After the affine reduction the surviving obligation quantifies
49	  over test *rings*; a field is a ring, so this is one instance of it and not the statement.
50	  The general-ring case needs a fibrewise-to-global argument (cohomology and base change) that
51	  this tree does not have, and nothing here supplies it.
52	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, and it does not claim to: at `genus C > 0` the
53	  hypothesis `genus C = 0` simply fails, and this file exhibits no positive-genus curve.
54	* **It does not produce a `JacobianData`** on its own.  The producer
55	  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` wants the ring-level hypothesis; the field case does
56	  not discharge it.
57	
58	## Main declarations
59	
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `χ(𝒪) = 1` at the
61	  base-changed curve, at every field extension, from `genus C = 0`.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero` — **the field-test
63	  layer**: at genus `0`, a relative Picard class of relative degree `0` over any field
64	  extension is trivial.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_eq_zero_iff_of_genus_zero` — the same as an iff.
66	-/

68	set_option autoImplicit false

70	universe u
71	
72	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
73	
74	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
75	
76	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
77	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
78	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
79	
80	-- The base-change instance stack of `Curve.BaseChangeInstances` is resolved twice here (both
81	-- Betti numbers), which exceeds the default budget; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap precedent.
82	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
83	/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1` at the base-changed curve**, at every field extension of the base, from
84	`genus C = 0`.
85	
86	Both Betti numbers transport: `h⁰` by `finrank_h0_baseField` composed with `h0_moduleKSheaf`
87	(which is `1` on any proper geometrically integral curve), and `h¹` by
88	`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus`.  So `χ = 1 - genus C`, which the hypothesis makes `1`. -/
89	theorem chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero
90	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0) :
91	    Sheaf.chi ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 := by
92	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
93	  have hh1 : Sheaf.h1 ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = genus C :=
94	    finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus C K
95	  have hh0 : Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K)
96	      = Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) := finrank_h0_baseField C K
97	  have hbase : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 := h0_moduleKSheaf C
98	  rw [Sheaf.chi, hh0, hbase, hh1, hg]
99	  norm_num
100	
101	-- Same base-change instance stack as the χ lemma above, plus the `relPic.ind` elimination.
102	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
103	/-- **THE FIELD-TEST LAYER**: at genus `0`, a relative Picard class of relative degree `0`
104	over any field extension of the base is trivial.
105	
106	`relPicDeg` is defined by descending `classDeg` along `relPicMk`, and `relPicDeg_relPicMk` is
107	`rfl`, so on a representative the hypothesis *is* `classDeg K L = 0` and the genus-`0`
108	converse applies at the base-changed curve. -/
109	theorem relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
110	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
111	    (y : relPic C (overSpec k K)) (hy : relPicDeg (C := C) K y = 0) : y = 1 := by
112	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 :=
113	    chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero C K hg
114	  induction y using relPic.ind with
115	  | mk L =>
116	    have hcl : classDeg K L = 0 := hy
117	    have hL1 : L = 1 := eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one K hchi L hcl
118	    rw [hL1, map_one]
119	
120	-- Carries the same base-change instance stack through both directions.
121	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
122	/-- The iff form: at genus `0` the relative degree over a field extension vanishes exactly on
123	the trivial class.  The reverse direction is `map_one`. -/
124	theorem relPicDeg_eq_zero_iff_of_genus_zero
125	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hg : genus C = 0)
126	    (y : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
127	    relPicDeg (C := C) K y = 0 ↔ y = 1 :=
128	  ⟨relPic_eq_one_of_relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_genus_zero C K hg y, fun h => by
129	    subst h
130	    exact map_zero (relPicDeg (C := C) K)⟩
131	
132	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES AT GENUS `0` ON A FIBREWISE-TRIVIAL CLASS, OVER A TEST RING
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance of the degree-zero
13	Picard vanishing at genus `0`; `Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T`
14	binder *is* the `∀` test-ring binder.  What remained was the **ring** case, and the note
15	released with it priced that as "cohomology and base change, absent from this tree".
16	
17	**That price was wrong, and this file is the correction.**  The relevant engine is landed and
18	is stated over an arbitrary test ring for an arbitrary class:
19	
20	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301` — every Čech Picard class on `C_B` is
21	  `D.cechPicClass` for some `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π`, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`;
22	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean:198` — `datumRigidEngine`: from a *fibrewise* `H¹`
23	  hypothesis, `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` is finite projective over `B`;
24	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafDatumFibre.lean:169` — the fibrewise hypothesis follows from a
25	  witness divisor on the fibre curve with vanishing `H¹`;
26	* `Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:148` — on the vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` and
27	  `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1`.
28	
29	What nobody had connected is that at **genus `0`** the fibre inputs of that chain are *free*
30	rather than expensive, and this file proves exactly that.
31	
32	## The two results, and why the hypothesis is the cheap one
33	
34	The fibre witness is the **zero divisor**.  Its class is `1` (`picClass_zero`) and its sheaf is
35	the structure sheaf (`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso`), whose `H¹` has `K`-dimension
36	`genus C` at every field extension `K/k` (`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus`) — so at genus `0` it
37	vanishes, at every prime of `B` at once, with no locus, no openness argument and no
38	spreading-out.  Hence:
39	
40	* `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero` — the engine's `hfib` clause, for **any**
41	  datum whose fibre classes are trivial;
42	* `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `H⁰` of stalk rank `1` at every prime,
43	  i.e. `π_*L` invertible in the rank spelling, with `χ = 1` supplied by `genus C = 0` rather
44	  than assumed.
45	
46	**The hypothesis is fibre-class triviality, not fibre degree.**  That spelling is deliberate
47	and is not a strengthening in disguise: at genus `0` the two are *equivalent* by the landed
48	field-level converse (`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`), and
49	`fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` below is that equivalence at this site.  The
50	reason to state the theorems on triviality is mechanical, and worth recording because it will
51	bite the next lane: `classDeg K` carries five instance binders on the fibre curve
52	(`IsIntegral`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `QuasiCompact`, and both `Module.Finite`
53	Betti-number clauses) which do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so a
54	hypothesis phrased `∀ p, classDeg κ(p) … = 0` **cannot be stated** at a general prime without
55	`haveI`-installing them first — measured, not guessed.  Triviality of the class needs none of
56	them.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	* **It does not discharge the `pic⁰` vanishing at a test ring.**  It supplies the two
61	  cohomological outputs — `H¹ = 0` and `H⁰` invertible — that the classical proof consumes
62	  next through the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`.  That map does not exist in this tree, in the
63	  sibling project, or in mathlib (measured this session), so the remaining distance is a
64	  *different* argument and is not shortened by anything proved here.
65	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, where the fibre `H¹` is genuinely nonzero and the
66	  witness above fails at the first step.
67	* It introduces **no hypothesis on the curve** beyond the three standing binders and
68	  `genus C = 0`, and no hypothesis on the test ring beyond `IsNoetherianRing` — which
69	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove and which a consumer should remove
70	  through that route rather than by re-proving anything here.
71	
72	## Main declarations
73	
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero`
75	  — **the engine's fibrewise hypothesis, free at genus `0`**.
76	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero` — the engine's three
77	  conclusions with the fibrewise clause discharged.
78	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` —
79	  **`H⁰` of stalk rank `1`**, at every prime.
80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` — the
81	  degree-`0` spelling of the hypothesis implies the triviality spelling, so nothing is lost by
82	  stating the results on the latter.
83	-/

139	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)

152	theorem rigidEngine_of_genus_zero (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
153	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)

155	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :

172	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
173	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,

179	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1

181	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
182	  haveI : QuasiCompact
183	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
184	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
185	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
186	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
187	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
188	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
189	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=

206	theorem fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero
207	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
208	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
209	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1

10	/-!
11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
15	
16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
17	
18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
21	anywhere in the statement.
22	
23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
24	
25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
26	
27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
43	
44	## What this buys, stated exactly
45	
46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
51	this tree.
52	
53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
60	
61	## What this does NOT do
62	
63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
77	
78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
82	
83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
92	
93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
99	
100	## Main declarations
101	
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
112	  arbitrary field.
113	-/

190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`

193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
198	triviality at genus `0`.

201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule

221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField

224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _

235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :

263	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) holds at an arbitrary test **ring**, so for a `pic⁰` class whose

271	`exists_datum_pic0_presentation` upgrades it to the datum form. -/

273	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
274	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
275	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
276	      picEtAffineEquiv C B (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z)
277	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) :=
278	  exists_datum_pic0_presentation C B π _ ⟨z, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C B z⟩

281	relative Picard class over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring, at genus `0`.
282	
283	This is the form the earlier statements should have had: the only hypotheses left are the
284	membership itself, that the class comes from `relPic` (`hz`), the covering datum and the
285	engine's `IsNoetherianRing`.  The datum is existentially produced rather than supplied.

294	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
295	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
296	    (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
297	    (hg : genus C = 0) (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
298	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B))
299	    (hz : (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B)) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z) :
300	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
301	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
302	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := presentation_of_relPicToPicEt C B π z
303	  exact ⟨D, fun p => D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ hg lam (by rw [hz]; exact hD) p⟩

314	    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
315	    {π : (P1.asOver k).left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
316	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum (P1.asOver k) B π)
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = (P1.asOver k).hom)
318	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
319	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) B (lam : picEt (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))

10	# A `pic⁰` CLASS OVER A TEST **RING** IS TRIVIAL ON EVERY FIBRE
11	
12	The one surviving instance of the hypothesis both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through
13	is the **ring** case of the degree-zero vanishing:
14	
15	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
16	
17	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance at genus `0`, and
18	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the affine binder *is* the `∀ T` binder.  What
19	separates the two is a rigidity statement over a base ring, and the classical route to it —
20	cohomology and base change — consumes a **fibrewise** hypothesis.
21	
22	**This file supplies that hypothesis, as a theorem rather than a binder.**  For a `pic⁰` class
23	over an arbitrary test ring `A`, at genus `0`:
24	
25	* its restriction along every field point of `overSpec k A` is `1` (`fibre_eq_one`);
26	* its fibre Čech class at every prime `p` of `A` has `classDeg κ(p) = 0`
27	  (`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`, via the DAT-4 seam).
28	
29	## SUPERSEDED IN PART — read this before citing the first two theorems
30	
31	A fresh-context audit of this file (accepted in full) established two things about its own
32	content, and both are recorded here rather than in a commit message nobody reads:
33	
34	1. **`Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean:104` has the same statement at an ARBITRARY
35	   test object.**  `fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` is `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`
36	   without the affineness of the test, by the same `Subsingleton.elim`, and it landed twenty
37	   minutes after this file.  So the first two theorems below are *affine specializations of a
38	   landed more general lemma* and should not be cited as independent results; cite that one.
39	   The residue-field corollary is a one-line instantiation of it too.
40	2. **The lead theorem's proof does not use its own subject.**  `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`
41	   is `Subsingleton.elim` on the target group, so `lam`, `t` and `pic0Map` appear in the
42	   statement and contribute nothing to the proof — the probe replacing the subject by an
43	   arbitrary element of the target closes identically.  The "mechanism" the docstring below
44	   describes (`pic0Map` landing in `pic0Subgroup` through `degAt_picEtMap`) is work done by the
45	   *type ascription*, not by the proof term.  That is not a defect in the statement, which is
46	   true and is the shape consumers want; it does mean the theorem is cheap, and it was first
47	   presented here as though the mechanism were the content.
48	
49	**What survives as this file's own contribution** is the third theorem,
50	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`: the DAT-4 seam application that turns the
51	membership into a *degree* equation at each prime, which is the spelling
52	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` consumes.  It is two tactic lines and it is not duplicated.
53	
54	## What consumes this, and in which spelling
55	
56	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine on a
57	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under exactly
58	
59	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
60	
61	and its own `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts a *degree-`0`* hypothesis at
62	a prime into that triviality at genus `0`.  So the engine's binder is reachable from a `pic⁰`
63	membership, and this file is the reduction that reaches it: `htriv_of_pic0` composes the two.
64	
65	The residue-field instantiation is written out and is **not** a restatement of the field-point
66	form: `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps `A →ₐ[k] K` into fields, and the
67	engine quantifies over primes of `A`.  A prime's residue field is such a `K` and
68	`IsLocalRing.residue ∘ algebraMap` such a map, but the instantiation has to be written for the
69	consumer to fire — recorded because the two spellings look interchangeable and are not
70	(the caveat pic-c raised on `I-1640`).
71	
72	## Why the degree condition is *entirely* consumed here
73	
74	Membership in `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` is degree vanishing at every field point.  The
75	*triviality* statements spend that binder and return a conclusion with no degree in it, so the
76	distance from them to the ring case carries no Riemann–Roch, no `χ`, no chart and no divisor: it
77	is the pure rigidity implication "trivial at every fibre ⟹ trivial".  That is a repricing of the
78	ring case, not a discharge of it.
79	
80	**Corrected after audit:** this claim is *false about the third theorem*, and an earlier version
81	of this paragraph asserted it of every statement in the file.
82	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` has a degree equation **in its conclusion** — that
83	is its purpose, since the engine's converse consumes a degree — and it takes no `genus C = 0`
84	binder at all, so the sentence "both statements consume `genus C = 0`" was wrong about it as
85	well.  Three of the four theorems consume the genus; the degree one does not.
86	
87	## What this does NOT do
88	
89	* **It does not prove the ring case.**  Fibrewise triviality is strictly weaker than triviality
90	  over `A`: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails to synthesize even *given*
91	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` (measured, `lake env lean`), so no chart or fibre argument
92	  closes the gap by itself; Traverso–Swan is why.  What closes it is the rigid engine's
93	  invertibility conclusion plus a section, which is another lane's route.
94	* **The `classDeg` statement is conditional on a cocycle presentation** of the class
95	  (`h : picEtAffineEquiv C A lam = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C _ L)`), because the DAT-4 seam
96	  is.  `fibre_eq_one` is unconditional.
97	* **Nothing here is about positive genus.**  Both statements consume `genus C = 0` through the
98	  landed field-test vanishing; at positive genus the fibre classes are *not* trivial and the
99	  conclusion is false.
100	
101	## Main declarations
102	
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — **the fibrewise triviality**: a `pic⁰`
104	  class over a test ring restricts to `1` at every field point, at genus `0`.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — the same at the residue
106	  field of a prime, the spelling the ring-datum engine quantifies over.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` — the fibre Čech class of a
108	  cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree `0` at every prime.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one` — non-vacuity: the same at `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary
110	  field, with no hypothesis at all.
111	-/
112	
113	set_option autoImplicit false
114	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
115	
116	universe u
117	
118	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory Opposite
119	
120	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
121	
122	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
123	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
124	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
125	
126	noncomputable section
127	
128	/-! ## Fibrewise triviality of a degree-zero class over a test ring -/
129	
130	/-- **A `pic⁰` class over a test RING is trivial at every field point**, at `genus C = 0`.
131	
132	The mechanism is that `pic0Map` *lands in* `pic0Subgroup` at the target test — the degree-zero
133	condition is stable under restriction, definitionally through `degAt_picEtMap`
134	(`Pic0Functor.lean:87`).  At a **field** test the whole degree-zero subgroup is a subsingleton
135	(`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`), so the restricted class equals `1`
136	there.
137	
138	This consumes the degree binder completely: the conclusion mentions no degree.  It is the
139	fibrewise hypothesis of cohomology-and-base-change, available at genus `0` for *every* class at
140	*every* prime simultaneously — no locus, no openness, no spreading-out. -/
141	theorem pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
142	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
143	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
144	    pic0Map C t lam = 1 :=
145	  @Subsingleton.elim _
146	    (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero C K hg) _ _
147	
148	/-- The same in the underlying `picEt` group: the restricted class is the trivial class. -/
149	theorem picEtMap_pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
150	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
151	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
152	    picEtMap C t (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) = 1 :=
153	  fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup C hg lam K t
154	
155	/-! ## The residue-field spelling: what the ring-datum engine quantifies over -/
156	
157	/-- **The fibrewise triviality at the residue field of a prime.**
158	
159	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` quantifies its `htriv` binder over `PrimeSpectrum B`, while
160	`pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps into fields.  A prime's residue field
161	`κ(p)` is a field extension of `k` (through `A`), and the field point of `overSpec k A` at `p` is
162	`Over.overSpecMap` of the composite algebra map — so the two quantifiers match, but only once
163	this instantiation is written.
164	
165	Recorded as its own declaration for exactly that reason: "residue fields are field points" is
166	true and is not a proof that a consumer indexed by primes can fire. -/
167	theorem pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
168	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
169	    (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
170	    pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap
171	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
172	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero C hg lam _ _
173	
174	/-! ## The degree of the fibre Čech class -/
175	
176	/-- **The fibre Čech class of a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree zero**, at every
177	`k`-algebra map into a field — in particular at every residue field.
178	
179	Route: the DAT-4 seam `degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk` (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`)
180	identifies `degAt lam (Over.overSpecMap φ)` with `classDeg K` of the pulled-back Čech class, and
181	membership in `pic0Subgroup` says the left side is `0`.
182	
183	This is the form a consumer holding a *degree* hypothesis at a prime wants: the ring-datum
184	engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts it to triviality of the fibre
185	class at genus `0`. -/
186	theorem classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented
187	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
188	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic)
189	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C A (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A))
190	      = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L))
191	    (φ : A →ₐ[k] K) :
192	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) = 0 := by
193	  rw [← degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk φ (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) L h]
194	  exact lam.2 K (Over.overSpecMap φ)
195	
196	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statements fire at a curve, unconditionally -/
197	
198	/-- **Fibrewise triviality at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
199	
200	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field and
201	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` the three curve binders, so the theorem above applies with nothing left to
202	discharge.  Recorded because a fibrewise hypothesis nobody can instantiate is worth nothing, and
203	this one is instantiated at a real curve over an arbitrary field. -/
204	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
205	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
206	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A))
207	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
208	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) t lam = 1 :=
209	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam K t
210	
211	/-- Non-vacuity of the residue-field spelling at `ℙ¹`. -/
212	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
213	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
214	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A)) (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
215	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) (Over.overSpecMap
216	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
217	  pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam p
218	
219	end

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FamilyCoboundary

9	/-!
10	# A LOCAL-EQUATION SYSTEM OF UNITS PRESENTS THE TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS
11	
12	`Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass` (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean:238`) is the Čech class of the
13	cocycle of transition units `g x y = eqn x / eqn y`.  The landed API around it computes the
14	class *from* a system in every direction except one: **nothing concluded that a class is
15	trivial**.  The producers of `picClass … = 1` were `picClass_zero` (the zero *divisor*, a
16	different carrier) and `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (which only transports triviality between two
17	systems, never establishes it).
18	
19	This file supplies the missing producer, and it is generic: no curve, no base ring, no
20	degree, no cohomology.
21	
22	  **`eqn x` a unit at every point ⟹ `picClass = 1`.**
23	
24	## The mechanism, and why it is not the obvious `simp`
25	
26	The defining relation `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` (`eqn_restrict_eq`) says exactly that the family
27	`α x := (eqn x)⁻¹` is a **coboundary datum** for the transition cocycle, once every `eqn x` is
28	invertible.  `Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family` (`Picard/FamilyCoboundary.lean:107`) turns a
29	coboundary datum on a refining family into triviality of the `H¹` class, and here the refining
30	family is the cover itself — index type `X`, opens `d.cover.opens`, refinement `le_rfl`.
31	
32	Two mechanical points, recorded because they cost time and will cost it again:
33	
34	* the family lemma restricts the cocycle along `inf_le_inf le_rfl le_rfl`, so the proof needs
35	  "restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity".  That is `Scheme.resHom_refl` on sections, but a
36	  `rw` with a `unitsRestrict`-level version **fails to match** — the `le`-witness sits inside a
37	  proof argument and the rewrite motive is not type-correct at `instances` transparency.  The
38	  fix that works is to `have` the identity with the inequality *universally quantified*
39	  (`hself` below), so unification picks the witness rather than matching it;
40	* `Scheme.CechPic.mk_one` supplies the `1` in the class group on the same cover, so the two
41	  sides are `mk` of the same cover and `congr 1` reduces to the `unitsH1` statement.
42	
43	## What consumes it, immediately
44	
45	`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroGeneral.lean` proves, over an **arbitrary** test ring, that a
46	degree-`0` certified adaptation has unit equations
47	(`isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero`) and is `DivEq` to the trivial system
48	(`divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero`).  Until now that chain ended at `DivEq`, i.e. at the
49	*quotient* carrier `DivFam`, and said nothing about the **class** in `CechPic` — which is the
50	object the `pic⁰` vanishing is about.  Composing with the theorem here closes that gap:
51	
52	  **a degree-`0` certified divisor family has trivial Picard class, at every test ring.**
53	
54	That is `picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero` below, and it needs no field, no integrality, no
55	smoothness and no Noetherian hypothesis — it inherits exactly the hypotheses of the landed
56	degree-`0` certificate lemma.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	* **It does not prove the `pic⁰` vanishing over a ring.**  The gap that remains there is the
61	  *converse* production step: given a degree-`0` class on `C_A`, exhibit a certified family
62	  presenting it.  The field case of that is `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq`
63	  (`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`) and it is field-only; over a ring the section
64	  route (`Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:248` then
65	  `Picard/SectionsToDivisorsClass.lean:212`) is the live candidate and is not completed here.
66	* It says nothing about `picFromBase` membership, which is the `relPic`-level statement and a
67	  strictly weaker conclusion than `picClass = 1` in `CechPic`.
68	
69	## Main declarations
70	
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn` — **the keystone**:
72	  unit equations present the trivial class.  Generic in the scheme.
73	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns` — the trivial system has trivial class.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero` — **a degree-`0`
75	  certified system has trivial class, at every test ring**.
76	-/
77	
78	set_option autoImplicit false
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory Limits
83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
85	
86	/-! ## The keystone, generic in the scheme -/
87	
88	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
89	
90	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	
92	/-- **A LOCAL-EQUATION SYSTEM OF UNITS PRESENTS THE TRIVIAL CLASS.**
93	
94	The defining relation `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` says the family `α x := (eqn x)⁻¹` is a
95	coboundary datum for the transition cocycle; `Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family` on the cover
96	itself (index type `X`, refinement `le_rfl`) converts that into triviality of the `H¹` class,
97	and `CechPic.mk_one` puts the two sides on the same cover.
98	
99	This is the only producer of `picClass … = 1` in the tree that establishes triviality rather
100	than transporting it: `picClass_eq_of_divEq` moves it between systems and `picClass_zero` is
101	about the zero *divisor*, a different carrier. -/
102	theorem picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn (d : X.LocalEquations)
103	    (hu : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (d.eqn x)) : d.picClass = 1 := by
104	  rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass, show (1 : X.CechPic)
105	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk d.cover 1 from (Scheme.CechPic.mk_one d.cover).symm]
106	  congr 1
107	  refine Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family d.unitsCocycle (fun x => x) d.cover.opens
108	    (fun _ => le_rfl) (fun x => ⟨x, d.cover.mem_opens x⟩)
109	    (fun x => (hu x).unit⁻¹) ?_
110	  intro x y
111	  -- Restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity.  The inequality must stay *quantified*: with a
112	  -- fixed witness the `rw` motive is not type-correct at `instances` transparency.
113	  have hself : ∀ (h : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)
114	      (w : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ), X.unitsRestrict h w = w :=
115	    fun h w => Units.ext (X.resHom_refl (w : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)))
116	  -- The unit form of `eqn_restrict_eq`: `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` as an identity of units.
117	  have key : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens x)
118	        (hu x).unit
119	      = d.ratioUnit x y * X.unitsRestrict
120	        (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens y) (hu y).unit :=
121	    Units.ext (by
122	      rw [Units.val_mul, Scheme.coe_unitsRestrict, Scheme.coe_unitsRestrict,
123	        IsUnit.unit_spec, IsUnit.unit_spec]
124	      exact d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
125	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, Scheme.LocalEquations.unitsCocycle_evInf, hself, key]
126	  group
127	
128	end Scheme.LocalEquations
129	
130	/-! ## The degree-`0` consequence, at every test ring -/
131	
132	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
133	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
134	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
135	
136	/-- **The trivial system has trivial Picard class.**  Its equations are literally `1`. -/
137	theorem DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns : (DivFamZar.trivEqns C R).picClass = 1 :=
138	  Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn _ fun y => by
139	    rw [DivFamZar.trivEqns_eqn]
140	    exact isUnit_one
141	
142	/-- **A DEGREE-`0` CERTIFIED SYSTEM HAS TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS, AT EVERY TEST RING.**
143	
144	`isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroGeneral.lean:125`) spends the
145	degree-`0` rank clause on making every *chart* equation a unit; `eqn_rel` then makes the
146	system's own equations units on the piece overlaps, which is what
147	`divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero` packages as `DivEq` with the trivial system.  Composing
148	that with `picClass_eq_of_divEq` and the class of the trivial system gives the statement at the
149	level of `CechPic`, which is where the `pic⁰` vanishing lives — the landed chain stopped at the
150	`DivFam` quotient.
151	
152	Hypotheses are exactly the landed lemma's: **no field, no integrality, no smoothness, no
153	Noetherian ring.** -/
154	theorem DivisorAdaptation.picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero
155	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
156	    (hc : A.IsCertified 0) : d.picClass = 1 :=
157	  (Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq
158	    (A.divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero hc)).trans DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns
159	
160	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
10	
11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
13	instance
14	
15	```
16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
17	```
18	
19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
23	
24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
25	
26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
29	
30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
34	`Sigma.desc`.
35	
36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
39	
40	## The honest scope, stated up front
41	
42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
46	none to check.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
72	
73	noncomputable section
74	
75	variable (C) in
76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
77	
78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
80	
81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
90	
91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
93	
94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
97	covering sieve is covering.
98	
99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
114	
115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
116	
117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
122	
123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
129	  intro T s
130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
132	  intro T' g _
133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
134	
135	end
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry
